requiredDocumentFields.label: Buyer reference (Leitweg-ID)
requiredDocumentFields.why: § 5 ERechV: "Die elektronische Rechnung hat neben den umsatzsteuerrechtlichen Rechnungsbestandteilen mindestens folgende Angaben zu enthalten: 1. eine Leitweg-Identifikationsnummer, [...]" — a Leitweg-ID is a MANDATORY invoice component under federal law, not optional the way France's own "code service" is (see fr.json's own entry). Carried generically as `data.buyerReference` (`formats/shared-build.ts#extractBuyerReference`), the SAME field the `country-fields/data/de.json` overlay's own Leitweg-ID input feeds — see that file's own header.

provenance.sourceText: § 4 Abs. 1 ERechV (Verordnung über die elektronische Rechnungsstellung im öffentlichen Auftragswesen des Bundes): « Für die Ausstellung von elektronischen Rechnungen haben Rechnungssteller und Rechnungssender grundsätzlich den Datenaustauschstandard XRechnung vom 29. September 2017 (BAnz AT 10.10.2017 B1) in der jeweils aktuellen Fassung zu verwenden. » § 4 Abs. 3 ERechV: « Für die Übermittlung von elektronischen Rechnungen haben Rechnungssteller und Rechnungssender ein Verwaltungsportal des Bundes im Sinne von § 2 Absatz 2 des Onlinezugangsgesetzes zu nutzen. Voraussetzung für die Übermittlung einer elektronischen Rechnung ist, dass der Rechnungssteller oder Rechnungssender sich zuvor mit einem Nutzerkonto im Sinne von § 2 Absatz 5 des Onlinezugangsgesetzes registriert. » § 5 ERechV: « Die elektronische Rechnung hat neben den umsatzsteuerrechtlichen Rechnungsbestandteilen mindestens folgende Angaben zu enthalten: 1. eine Leitweg-Identifikationsnummer, 2. die Bankverbindungsdaten, 3. die Zahlungsbedingungen und 4. die De-Mail-Adresse oder eine E-Mail-Adresse des Rechnungsstellers. »

rule.notes:
READ DIRECTLY on 2026-09-01 at gesetze-im-internet.de (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/erechv/__4.html and .../__5.html — verbatim citations above, extracted from the official German text itself). EUROPEAN BASELINE: directive 2014/55/EU, art. 7 (see fr.json's own note for the full citation — the same baseline applies to all three countries in this wave). DECISION ON THE TRANSPORT — SETTLED BY READING, NOT GUESSED: the text read (§ 4 Abs. 3 ERechV) explicitly REQUIRES a deposit via "ein Verwaltungsportal des Bundes" (a FEDERAL administrative portal within the meaning of the Onlinezugangsgesetz — the "OZG"), with prior registration via a "Nutzerkonto" — this is neither a plain e-mail send nor a channel already implemented in this repository (email/pdp/ksef/sdi). `transportId: "zre-ozgre"` therefore DELIBERATELY references the two federal platforms actually known under these names (ZRE — Zentrale Rechnungseingangsplattform des Bundes; OZG-RE — the shared OZG platform for the Länder that joined it), which do NOT EXIST in `transports/transport-registry.ts` — the exact same thesis as the French "chorus-pro" block (see fr.json's own note and actions/invoice-actions.ts's own header): sending an invoice by e-mail to a German federal public entity does NOT SATISFY the text above (which requires the PORTAL, not merely the XRechnung format), so silently routing to "email" would do exactly what this project refuses elsewhere (serve an artifact that LOOKS compliant — the right XML format — without going through the channel the law actually mandates). Sending therefore blocked, by naming it, until a ZRE/OZG-RE channel (or Peppol, if ever adopted as an alternative) was actually implemented — it was PEPPOL that was adopted and wired, see the ADDENDUM 2026-09-02 below for the full resolution. ASSUMED LIMITATION: the ERechV read here is the FEDERAL (Bund) text — each of Germany's 16 Länder has its own e-invoicing ordinance, potentially different (its own portal, or even a less strict channel); this rule covers ONLY what a uniform federal text allows asserting for the whole country, never an average or an assumption about the Länder — settling that would mean reading all 16 regional texts one by one, out of this task's scope. — ADDENDUM 2026-09-02 (wiring the 'peppol' transport — RESOLVED): READ DIRECTLY at https://www.e-rechnung-bund.de/faq/ (official site, operated by the Beschaffungsamt des BMI — the federal Ministry of the Interior's own procurement office): since September 2025, ZRE and OZG-RE have MERGED into a single platform (« Ein Jahr nach der Zusammenführung von ZRE und OZG-RE »), and this merged platform explicitly lists Peppol as ONE of its official deposit channels, alongside web entry, upload, and e-mail: « Die OZG-RE bietet als weiteren Übertragungskanal die Möglichkeit zum Rechnungsversand aus der erstellenden Software mittels Übertragung über das Peppol-Netzwerk an. » ("OZG-RE offers, as a further transmission channel, the possibility of sending an invoice from the issuing software via the Peppol network."). WHAT STILL BLOCKED AS OF THAT DATE: this repository's `peppol` transport (`transports/peppol-transport.ts`) built EXCLUSIVELY a generic Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 artifact (`formats/peppol-bis-provider.ts`), never an XRechnung one (`formats/xrechnung-provider.ts`) — yet § 4 Abs. 1 ERechV cited above explicitly requires XRechnung as the CONTENT, independent of which transmission channel is used; silently routing to `peppol` would have delivered generic Peppol-BIS content over a recognized-compliant channel, with no way for this repository to claim that content itself satisfies XRechnung. RESOLVED BY THIS TASK: `transports/transport-registry.ts#DocumentTransportContext` now carries an optional `formatOverride`; `actions/invoice-actions.ts#resolveB2gInvoiceTransport` sets it to THIS rule's own `formatSyntax` ("xrechnung") whenever a B2G rule selects the transport; `transports/peppol-transport.ts#resolveFormatForSend` honors it by building `xrechnungFormatProvider` instead of the default `peppolBisFormatProvider`, and refuses BY NAME (never a silent fallback to Peppol BIS) if an override with no wired provider were ever requested — a fixed-format transport (chorus-pro, sdi, face, anaf, email) ignores this field with no effect, proven by regression on each one's EXISTING tests. Proven by `formats/xrechnung-provider.spec.ts`'s own master proof (the XRechnung CustomizationID, never the Peppol BIS one, in the produced XML) AND, at the full-service level (B2G preflight → worker → Access Point call), by `actions/invoice-b2g-de-peppol-send.spec.ts`: the payload ACTUALLY sent to the Access Point carries `urn:...:xrechnung_3.0`, never `urn:...:poacc:billing:3.0`. `transportId` therefore moves from `zre-ozgre` to `peppol`.

PEPPOL ADDRESSING OF THE GERMAN PUBLIC RECIPIENT (⚖, READ, not guessed): the official Peppol "Participant Identifier Schemes" code list v9.7 (https://docs.peppol.eu/edelivery/codelists/, file "Peppol Code Lists - Participant identifier schemes v9.7.json", checked 2026-09-02) lists ISO 6523 code `0204` as `schemeid: "DE:LWID"`, `scheme-name: "Peppol-Leitweg-ID"`, `country: "DE"`, `issuing-agency: "Koordinierungsstelle für IT-Standards (KoSIT)"`, `state: "active"`. The same e-rechnung-bund.de/faq/ page cited above confirms this plainly, verbatim, in the section « Wie hängen die Peppol-Participant-ID und die Leitweg-ID zusammen? »: « Präfix 0204 + Leitweg-ID → 0204:Leitweg-ID », and gives a concrete example for its own test sandbox (section « Wie kann ich Testrechnungen via Peppol an die OZG-RE senden? »): « Peppol-Receiver-ID: 0204:99661-WEBSERVICEOZG-28 ». DECISION ON WHERE THE CLIENT-SIDE PARTICIPANT ID COMES FROM: this repository ALREADY carries a generic mechanism for this fact — the client's own `PEPPOL_ENDPOINT` identifier (`client-upsert.tsx`'s own "Peppol / Electronic routing" section, "{schemeId}:{endpointId}"), read directly by `transports/peppol-transport.ts#send()` (never guessed) — so the user enters `0204:<their Leitweg-ID>` there for a German public client, exactly the same mechanism a client from any other country uses to enter their own Peppol scheme. DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED to `requiredClientIdentifiers` above (unlike the French SIRET or the Italian Codice Univoco): `PEPPOL_ENDPOINT` has, on the client screen (`client-upsert.tsx`, read during this task), its OWN dedicated section ("Peppol / Electronic routing"), distinct from the generic "country identifiers" list that `requiredClientIdentifiers` feeds on that screen (that component's own `requiredIdentifiers` merge) — duplicating it there would have produced TWO fields for the same fact (one in the generic list, never filled in by a user who fills in the other dedicated section instead) and a submit-time validation pointing at the wrong field: a concrete screen defect, found by reading this file, not a guess. The NAMED refusal when it is missing therefore stays carried by the EXISTING, already-generic mechanism in `peppol-transport.ts#send()` ("this client has no Peppol endpoint on file"), never duplicated here — see `actions/invoice-b2g-de-peppol-send.spec.ts`'s own proof that this refusal does hold for a German GOVERNMENT client routed by THIS rule, not only for an ordinary B2B Peppol send.

LIVE (⚖, attempted and SUCCEEDED on 2026-09-02, raw result): `peppol/peppol-sh-xrechnung.live.spec.ts` reuses the pattern of the already-proven Peppol BIS round-trip (peppol.sh BE company + explicit `peppol_id`, `FR` always rejected with `invalid_country`), but builds and sends an XRechnung (`xrechnungFormatProvider`, German seller WITH an IBAN for BR-DE-1) instead of a Peppol BIS document. Result: `doc_v37PTxYOQGn78bPAnMiI0` → `QUEUED` → `DELIVERED` in a single poll step (~10 s) — see documentation/docs/developer-guide/live-testing.md for the full detail. HONEST LIMIT of this green, read in `peppol-sh-client.ts#ublToPeppolShDocument`'s own header BEFORE over-interpreting it: peppol.sh NEVER accepts raw UBL bytes, it EXTRACTS a handful of generic fields (party/VAT/currency/dates/lines) and RE-SERIALIZES its own document server-side — its extraction reads neither `cbc:CustomizationID` nor any XRechnung-specific element. The `DELIVERED` therefore proves the XRechnung artifact is structurally compatible with the same generic extraction path as Peppol BIS, NOT that peppol.sh judges or retains the content as specifically XRechnung — the properly XRechnung-specific proof (the CustomizationID actually present in the bytes sent) is judged LOCALLY by this same spec, BEFORE sending, never by the network itself.

HONESTLY ACKNOWLEDGED LIMITS, NOT LIFTED BY THIS TASK: (1) the Peppol document-type identifier announced to the Access Point for this content (`PEPPOL_DOC_TYPES.INVOICE_XRECHNUNG_UBL`, `transports/peppol/peppol-client.ts`) MIRRORS the standard Peppol URN construction (the same `<CustomizationID>` actually written into the XML) but has NOT been independently verified against a real SMP record from OZG-RE itself — a point named, not guessed, at its own location (see this file's own header); (2) the Länder limitation from the previous paragraph remains entirely unchanged — nothing in this addendum lifts it.

— ADDENDUM 2026-09-15 (removal of the 'peppol' transport — PRODUCT DECISION, REVERSES THE 2026-09-02 ADDENDUM): the `peppol` transport was removed from the entire product, not just from this rule. Reason: this repository's generic client (`transports/peppol-transport.ts`, `transports/peppol/peppol-client.ts`) sent to `POST /api/v1/send`, a shape that matches NONE of the real Access Point providers this repository's own research identified (`documentation/docs/developer-guide/credentials-guide.md` §5, before its own removal) — this path therefore NEVER talked to a real production server, only to the free peppol.sh sandbox (see LIVE above), and proving it in production would have required a commercial account with an AP provider this project never had. Rather than keep a channel that would fail with the first real customer, the decision was to remove it entirely. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS RULE: `transportId` reverts to `zre-ozgre` — exactly the value and reasoning of the original entry above, before the 2026-09-02 addendum. `formatSyntax` stays `xrechnung`: the CONTENT obligation (§ 4 Abs. 1 ERechV) is a fact of the world, unchanged by this removal; only the CHANNEL disappears. A B2G send to a German public client therefore again returns the NAMED refusal « channel "zre-ozgre" not available in this deployment » (`actions/invoice-actions.ts#b2gTransportNotAvailableMessage`), never a silent send through another channel nor an obscure failure. WHAT IT WOULD TAKE TO RESTORE THIS ROUTE: (a) a real account with a commercial Peppol Access Point provider (a commercial step outside the code, on the operator's own account) with a `send()` that actually talks to it, rather than the `POST /api/v1/send` shape never validated against a real provider; or (b) a dedicated ZRE/OZG-RE client built against that federal platform's own real API. The `formatOverride` mechanism (`transport-registry.ts`'s own header) that carried the XRechnung build instead of Peppol BIS stays in place, dormant, for the day either of those exists.
